note: Generic HTTP Purger provides two Purge purger plugins - http (HttpPurger, one request per invalidation) and httpbundled (HttpBundledPurger, one request per batch) - both multi_instance. Each instance's config is a httppurgersettings config entity named purge_purger_http.settings.<id> with fields name, invalidationtype (default tag), hostname, port, path, request_method (default BAN), scheme, verify, headers, body, body_content_type, timeout, connect_timeout, cooldown_time, max_requests, runtime_measurement, http_errors. path/headers/body are token-aware (invalidation group for http, invalidations for httpbundled). A httpconfiguration diagnostic check validates enabled purgers. No configure route (edit via Purge purgers UI), no permissions, no Drush. Medium/hard cases are grounded in real httppurgersettings config entities.

evals.prompt: The purge_purger_http module adds HTTP-based Purge purgers. What are the ids of the two purger plugins it provides and how do they differ in how many HTTP requests they send?
evals.expected_output: http (HttpPurger) sends one HTTP request per invalidation instruction; httpbundled (HttpBundledPurger) sends a single request for a whole batch of invalidations. Both are multi-instance.

evals.prompt: For a purge_purger_http HTTP purger, what is the default HTTP request method and the default invalidation type, and what is the config object name that stores one instance's settings?
evals.expected_output: Default request_method is BAN and default invalidationtype is tag. Each instance is stored in the httppurgersettings config entity purge_purger_http.settings.<instance_id>.

evals.prompt: In purge_purger_http, how do you make the request path, a header value, or the body vary per cache-tag/URL being purged? Which token group does the single-item http purger expose versus the bundled one?
evals.expected_output: path, header values and body are run through Purge's token service, so you embed tokens (e.g. [invalidation:expression]). The http purger exposes the 'invalidation' token group (one item), while httpbundled exposes the 'invalidations' group (the whole batch).

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a purge_purger_http HTTP purger settings entity with id pph_known. Inspect its live configuration and state which HTTP request method it is configured to send.
On this site the purge_purger_http settings entity pph_known targets a cache host. Inspect its configuration and give the hostname it sends purge requests to.
evals.expected_output: Config purge_purger_http.settings.pph_known has hostname: cache.pphknown.test (port 80, scheme http).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, using the purge_purger_http module, configure an HTTP purger settings entity that sends PURGE requests to hostname pph-task.example.internal on port 80 over http, invalidating cache tags (invalidationtype tag). Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create a httppurgersettings config entity (purge_purger_http.settings.<id>) with hostname=pph-task.example.internal, request_method=PURGE, invalidationtype=tag (port 80, scheme http), e.g. via HttpPurgerSettings::create([...])->save().

evals.prompt: I have a caching proxy at pph-task.example.internal that clears content when it receives a PURGE request. Set up the Generic HTTP Purger so Drupal sends PURGE requests to that host to clear content by cache tag. Make it live on this site.
evals.expected_output: Same verified end state as purge_purger_http-build-purger: an HTTP purger settings entity targeting hostname pph-task.example.internal with request_method PURGE and invalidationtype tag.
